## Release Notes

Released on 2026-08-14.

### Python

- Add CPython 3.10.21, 3.11.16, and 3.12.14 ([#21138](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21138))
- Prefer newer versions and standard variants when selecting between equally prioritized Python interpreters ([#21134](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21134))

### Enhancements

- Simplify errors and hints for invalid editable requirements, and redact credentials in requirement URLs ([#21130](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21130))

### Preview features

- Allow `--index` and `--default-index` to select configured package indexes by name with the `index-by-name` preview feature ([#17455](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/17455))
- Include distribution artifact URLs and hashes in CycloneDX SBOM exports by default ([#21131](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21131))
- Fall back to logical file sizes when using `cache-physical-space` on filesystems that do not support physical-space accounting ([#21133](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21133))

### Bug fixes

- Resolve relative package index paths in PEP 723 scripts against the script directory ([#21097](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21097))

## Install uv 0.12.5

### Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.5/uv-installer.sh | sh
```

### Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

```sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.5/uv-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

## Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --repo astral-sh/uv
```

You can also download the attestation from [GitHub](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/attestations) and verify against that directly:
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --bundle <file-path of downloaded attestation>
```

signals.title: Sign published executables for macOS
signals.text: ### Summary The `uv` and `uvx` tools do not carry a code signature from Astral on macOS, as of version 0.8.2 checked on 2025-07-24 on macOS 15.5. ``` ❯ uv --version uv 0.8.2 (21fadbcc1 2025-07-22) ❯ sw_vers ProductName: macOS ProductVersion: 15.5 BuildVersion: 24F74 ``` I could not find a similar open or closed request regarding adding a macOS code signature to `uv` and `uvx` in the issue tracker. Issue #10366 is a similar request for Windows. Code signing from the developer is preferred and contributes to trust in these tools when running on macOS / Darwin. Code signing could potentially be done with other PKI, but for this request, the best result would be an Apple Developer ID signature. 1. Signing versions of `uv` and `uvx` on macOS would provide proof that the release came from Astral (or Astral’s build/release pipeline). CI/CD pipeline tools offer support for code signing actions. 2. The signature would enable verification that the tools have not been modified since their release. 3. The signature can be used in Apple’s anti-malware / threat protection processes. 4. The valid signature and its Team ID can be used by automation for IT teams, like [AutoPkg](https://github.com/autopkg/autopkg), to verify the downloaded releases when discovering new versions, packaging them, and preparing them for organizational deployments. Further, some organizations may either require apps/tools on macOS to carry a code signature from the developer, or encourage use of software with signatures over those without. ### Example Current signals.title: `uv sync` with `--no-editable` should force rebuild/install packages
signals.text: ### Summary When running `uv sync` with `--no-editable`, it seems like we'd expect that we re-install packages that would've been installed as editable (for example, the main package). Here's a simple example: ```shellsession jrosenth ~/example-project % uv init --build-backend uv Initialized project `example-project` jrosenth ~/example-project % uv sync --no-editable Using CPython 3.13.0 Creating virtual environment at: .venv Resolved 1 package in 2ms Built example-project @ file:///home/jrosenth/example-project Prepared 1 package in 15ms Installed 1 package in 1ms + example-project==0.1.0 (from file:///home/jrosenth/example-project) jrosenth ~/example-project % echo 'print("changed!")' >> src/example_project/__init__.py jrosenth ~/example-project % uv sync --no-editable Resolved 1 package in 0.88ms Audited 1 package in 0.04ms jrosenth ~/example-project % tail .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/example_project/__init__.py def main() -> None: print("Hello from example-project!") jrosenth ~/example-project % uv sync --no-editable --reinstall-package example-project Resolved 1 package in 0.94ms Built example-project @ file:///home/jrosenth/example-project Prepared 1 package in 15ms Uninstalled 1 package in 0.40ms Installed 1 package in 1ms ~ example-project==0.1.0 (from file:///home/jrosenth/example-project) jrosenth ~/example-project % tail .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/example_project/__init__.py def main() -> None: print("Hello from example-project!") print("changed!") ``` In this example, we notice the `example-project` package didn't sync local changes until `--reinstall-package` was manually used. With packages that have `path` dependencies, this could be a little bit more fishy, we'd expect each of those dependencies to re-build and re-install when `--no-editable` is applied. ### Platform Linux 6.15.8-arch1-2 x86_64 GNU/Linux ### Version uv 0.8.8 (9a54754b0 2025-08-08) ### Python version Python 3.13
signals.author: jackrosenthal

signals.title: uv sync and uv pip install fails for packages with console scripts when the venv contains a `lib` to `usr/lib` symlink
signals.text: ### Summary When a virtual environment directory contains a `lib` to `usr/lib` symlink, `uv` installs `console_scripts` entry points into `<venv>/usr/bin/<name>` instead of the venv's real scripts directory `<venv>/bin/<name>`. The launcher is *written* to a path relative to `site-packages` that traverses the `lib` symlink. This results in the following error: ``` error: Failed to install: idna-3.19-py3-none-any.whl (idna==3.19) Caused by: failed to query metadata of file `<venv>/bin/idna`: No such file or directory (os error 2) ``` ## Reproduction ```bash V=$(mktemp -d)/venv uv venv --allow-existing --python python3.12 "$V" mkdir -p "$V/usr/lib" "$V/usr/bin" ln -s usr/lib "$V/lib" # Install any package that ships a console script (idna provides `idna`). VIRTUAL_ENV="$V" uv pip install idna ls -l "$V/bin/idna" "$V/usr/bin/idna" ``` I suspect that this issue comes from the fact that after writing the console scripts, `uv` makes it executable and a recent change switched from using the relative path of `site_packages` to using the absolute_path: [ref](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/9a65753e9a8d0e99e7079114d78001311444c718#diff-f2224e4fc2200243c3f25811f8f3ea23cda624fab45a26a09f91c47d77aafdb7) ```rust // let path = site_packages.join(entrypoint_relative); let path = script.as_path(); let permissions = fs::metadata(path)?.permissions(); ``` ### Platform Ubuntu ### Version uv 0.12.0 ### Python version Python 3.12

signals.title: Add a `uv-dev wheel-replace` command
signals.text: Add `uv-dev wheel-replace` to replace explicitly selected wheel members after code signing and regenerate `RECORD` without introducing a second ZIP implementation. The command validates the input archive and hashes, rejects duplicate or unsafe members, preserves executable metadata, and writes the completed wheel atomically so release assembly can remain separate from the signing job. This is a precursor to #20623 which is an alternative to https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/18280 more in the vein of https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/18262 which I'm considering again because we do not want to put the code signing secrets on the runners we're using for builds.

signals.title: Preserve local path intent when merging dependency metadata
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #20477. When a project and one of its dependencies refer to the same local package, the path to that local package can end up mangled by backends etc. This means we could end up losing the original spelling from pyproject.toml which we use when creating the lockfile, thus making the result an absolute path. This PR handles merging this information properly, preferring the local metadata, so that the lockfile ends up with the right kind of path. ## Test Plan A regression test for the original issue, and some additional coverage because the fix was broadened to avoid this class of problems in general.
signals.author: EliteTK

signals.title: Support proxy indexes through reversible artifact URLs
signals.text: Add support for using a proxy for an existing package index without changing the URLs stored in lockfiles. Configure proxies on ordinary `[[tool.uv.index]]` or `[[index]]` entries with `proxy-for` and `artifact-base-url`. PyPI works without additional configuration; other indexes must specify where their artifacts are hosted. uv resolves and downloads packages through the proxy, but stores the original URLs in `uv.lock` and `pylock.toml`. When installing from an existing lockfile, it converts those original URLs back into proxy URLs. Authentication, errors, and caches belong to the proxy. Artifact hashes are checked before files are cached or written to lockfiles. Frozen and offline installs continue to work. ## Terminology - **Proxy index:** An index configured with `proxy-for` that serves packages for another index. - **Canonical index:** The original index whose identity and artifact URLs appear in lockfiles. - **Physical index:** The index uv contacts for requests, authentication, and caching. This is the proxy when one is configured. - **Artifact base URL:** The URL prefix where an index hosts package files, configured with `artifact-base-url`. - **Proxy route:** The connection between a canonical index and its physical index. - **Artifact URL mapping:** The reversible conversion between canonical and physical artifact URLs that preserves the path after each artifact base URL. ## Commit breakdown 1. **Define proxy indexes and reversible artifact routes.** Add the configuration options and schema. Validate proxy definitions, reject duplicates, support implicit PyPI, and map artifact URLs between the original index and its proxy. 2. **Route registry requests through proxies.** Send package and metadata requests to the proxy. Use its authentication settings, credentials, errors, and cache. Artifact hosts requiring separate credentials must specify them explicitly. 3. **Preserve canonical package URLs during proxy resolution.** Convert artifact URLs returned by the proxy into their original URLs before the resolver sees them. Keep artifact metadata and hashes, and reject URLs that cannot be mapped. 4. **Verify proxied distributions before caching or locking.** Convert original URLs back into proxy URLs for downloads and existing lockfiles. Check wheel and source hashes before caching, and require hashes when creating `uv.lock` or `pylock.toml`. 5. **Document and test proxy index workflows.** Document configuration and authentication. Test PyPI, authenticated endpoints, lockfiles, wheels, source distributions, frozen and offline installs, cache separation, duplicate definitions, unmapped artifacts, and hash failures.

signals.title: Reimplement `package.metadata`-less lockfiles
signals.text: The previous iterations of `package.metadata`-free lockfiles had missed a number of cases, and made it hard to ensure that all cases were actually covered. This PR takes a new approach: Remove the previous implementation, and then re-add it feature-by-feature in reviewable commit units. Each commit adds one feature that uv supports. The new approach is not entirely `package.metadata`-free, instead remote URL, which can activate other URL source, now have `package.metadata` which they previously didn't. That's required for offline validation (which is crucial for `uv lock --check` performance, offline or not) and IMO the more correct tradeoff: We shouldn't repeat information that's already available on disk, but we should state what we expect from remote resources. `uv.lock` revision 1.4 additionally records empty extras so `--frozen --extra foo` if the lock wasn't generated with extra `foo` present, but it was added to `pyproject.toml` afterwards. This is a lockfile size regression if you're using a lot of remote URLs, otherwise it's still a much smaller lockfile for large workspaces. Remote source are usually used sparingly as they are worse for performance, reliability and auditability than registry sources. ## Validation This change reflects basically every resolver assumption and form of dependency specification and also hits a number of preexisting bugs (see upstack PRs and skipped changes list). Instead of trying to reason through correctness from the features we're representing, this PR was tested (and fixed) against large, diverse validation set, checking that uv's invariants are upheld with lockfile revision 1.4. The PR is additionally split into one commit per feature the new freshness check support, to ease reviewing and ensure that all features are covered. The most import check that needs to always pass is `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` on a fresh lockfile. We don't need to check features such as `uv sync`, as `package.metadata` is only used for fast path freshness checks, and `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` exercises the offline fast path while blocking the slow path if it would use the internet (which is unacceptable both for performance and for checks that run in isolated environments). The goal is to cover the available dependency specification that people use, while not fixing unrelated bugs in this already large change. There are three of these larger validations. The first one is a script finds public GitHub projects with editable packages, workspaces, Git dependencies or dynamically generated dependencies and then verifies that both the original lockfile and a version with package metadata removed pass `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` inside an isolated docker container. This dataset contained 254 projects with 14k locked packages. The second validation uses the check-mode in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-ecosystem-testing with `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=lock-without-metadata` . The third one is running the test suite migrated to lockfile revision 1.4 with https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/4b98802626b18406a47e71fc2583bc5576934e6e, passing 4.8k tests: ``` features=test-python-patch,test-universal,native-auth cargo insta test --accept --test-runner nextest --workspace --features "$features" cargo nextest run --workspace --features "$features" ``` The PR handles the test cases and fixes from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/20803 too. The area with the least coverage wrt to its complexity is conflicts supports. While the support is implemented, I'd consider its current support much weaker than the rest of the features. ## Skipped changes The following independent bugfixes are deliberately excluded from this stack: - #21210. - #21225. The cache assertion remains a TODO here. The 4.8k-test run above included the add-cache fix and predates this extraction; it is not a fresh full-suite run of the reduced stack.

signals.title: Verify locked source archives before building metadata
signals.text: `uv.lock` records archive digests, but checking an existing lockfile or resolving with `--locked` can obtain source metadata without comparing those digests. A replaced source archive can therefore run its build backend before a later hash or lockfile check rejects it. Construct a `HashStrategy` from the existing lockfile's hashes for registry packages, direct URLs, and local archives. Enforce the recorded hashes when reusing cached source metadata, resolving with `--locked`, and installing build dependencies recorded in the lockfile into isolated build environments. Normalize equivalent archive subdirectories so they find the same recorded hashes. Keep recorded hashes while checking whether an existing lockfile is still usable, but allow unlocked fresh resolution to replace them. Build dependencies without recorded hashes remain allowed. Based on #21248, which checks source archives before saving them to the cache. #21246 contains the structural refactor, and #21247 separates hash generation from verification.

signals.title: Represent validated source archives before persistence
signals.text: Source archive helpers currently extract an archive and save it to the cache in the same call. Separate those steps so the type system records that extraction and its existing checks have completed before persistence. Introduce a private `ValidatedSourceArchive` that owns the temporary directory. Its HTTP and local constructors retain their transport setup, diagnostics, and cleanup behavior, while a private reader helper performs the shared extraction and hash collection. The consuming `persist` method saves the source tree and returns the collected hashes and byte count. This preserves existing behavior; it does not add trusted-hash comparisons or change cache repair. #21247 separates hash generation from verification, and #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before persistence.

signals.title: Separate hash generation policy from verification policy
signals.text: `HashStrategy` currently represents hash generation and verification as mutually exclusive choices. A resolution may need both: verify artifacts whose hashes have been supplied, while generating hashes for new artifacts. Store generation separately from `HashVerification` in `HashStrategy`. Each distribution still receives a `HashPolicy` specifying whether to generate or check hashes. Update existing call sites to use the separate settings while preserving their hash inputs and which hashes uv treats as trusted. Generation remains available for artifacts without supplied hashes, unless the caller requires a hash for every artifact. This does not read hashes from `uv.lock` or add new archive comparisons. Based on #21246. #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before source archives enter the cache. #21223 reads hashes from an existing `uv.lock` and supplies them for verification.
signals.author: zanieb

signals.title: Validate source archives before cache persistence
signals.text: Source archives can be saved to the cache before their caller-supplied hashes are checked. Cache repair can also save replacement contents before detecting a mismatch with the previous revision. Check supplied hashes alongside the existing download-size check in `ValidatedSourceArchive::extract`, before it returns the value consumed by `persist`. Check every digest from a previous revision there too, before a repaired source tree is saved. Extraction still streams into a private temporary directory and returns parser errors immediately. This also removes the split in persistence behavior captured by `ArchiveOrigin`. HTTP and local archives now accept `AlreadyExists` or `DirectoryNotEmpty` only when the destination is a directory, and both retain temporary-directory ownership through persistence. The HTTP path no longer calls `TempDir::keep` for archives with multiple top-level entries, so failed persistence attempts clean up those staged files too. HTTP response handling and local file opening remain separate, and cache locations and `rename_with_retry` are unchanged. The caller still supplies the hashes and any download size to check; this PR does not read trusted hashes from `uv.lock`. #21223 supplies the hashes recorded in an existing `uv.lock`. Based on #21247.

signals.title: Portable Environments
signals.text: ## Summary Add `--preview portable-envs` which makes relocatable environments backed by uv-managed Pythons "portable" or "real" environments which contain their own Python interpreter and can be moved between compatible machines. ## Notes Global `--preview` will enable this feature for all eligible environments. I think this might be a bit too much, but wasn't sure how to gate it. I am open for suggestions. This patches `libpython.dylib` to be relative to `@executable_path`. This means executables linking against `libpython` will work once they're in the virtual environment's `bin` directory, and will work when moved around. But executables not in the `bin` directory will _not_ work because `@executable_path` won't be in the right place. There's not much that can be done to fix this, AIUI... See also: #10598 This patches `_sysconfigdata_*.py` to make it portable. But it does it only for portable environments. I think it might be safe-ish to just do it always? signals.title: Preserve repository-relative Git archive paths during sync
signals.text: Fresh `uv sync` can look for a Git-hosted archive in the downstream project instead of the Git checkout, even though retrying with the written lockfile succeeds. Source history traces this to astral-sh/uv#10072: it introduced repository-relative `GitPathBuiltDist::install_path` and `GitPathSourceDist::install_path`, but their lock constructors applied `relative_to` against the workspace root and fell back to `std::path::absolute`. `locked_git_url` retained the original relative path, so the serialized lock was correct while the in-memory `GitSource.path` used by the first sync was not. The direct-archive tests locked before installing. Later, astral-sh/uv#19589 preserved Git identity when lowering generated metadata that references an archive in the same checkout, but its regression only inspected the lockfile. Neither exercised installation from the newly constructed in-memory lock. Preserve the repository-relative path in both Git archive lock constructors and use it consistently for `locked_git_url` and `GitSource.path`. The installer then resolves the archive inside the fetched Git checkout, so fresh sync and lockfile replay use the same path. Fixes astral-sh/uv#21244.

signals.title: Simplify Git filename ownership branches
signals.text: These Git source types only need ownership-specific handling when stripping the suffix after the final `@`: a borrowed filename can return a borrowed suffix, while an owned filename must own the extracted suffix. When no delimiter is present, both should return the original `Cow` unchanged, but the existing nested branches duplicate that case and obscure the allocation-preserving fallback. Use `if let` match guards for the delimiter cases and share the unchanged-filename fallback, preserving the existing filename extraction and ownership behavior.

signal.title: Validate source archives before cache persistence
signal.text: Source archives can be saved to the cache before their caller-supplied hashes are checked. Cache repair can also save replacement contents before detecting a mismatch with the previous revision. Check supplied hashes alongside the existing download-size check in `ValidatedSourceArchive::extract`, before it returns the value consumed by `persist`. Check every digest from a previous revision there too, before a repaired source tree is saved. Extraction still streams into a private temporary directory and returns parser errors immediately. This also removes the split in persistence behavior captured by `ArchiveOrigin`. HTTP and local archives now accept `AlreadyExists` or `DirectoryNotEmpty` only when the destination is a directory, and both retain temporary-directory ownership through persistence. The HTTP path no longer calls `TempDir::keep` for archives with multiple top-level entries, so failed persistence attempts clean up those staged files too. HTTP response handling and local file opening remain separate, and cache locations and `rename_with_retry` are unchanged. The caller still supplies the hashes and any download size to check; this PR does not read trusted hashes from `uv.lock`. #21223 supplies the hashes recorded in an existing `uv.lock`. Based on #21247.

signal.title: Verify locked source archives before building metadata
signal.text: `uv.lock` records archive digests, but checking an existing lockfile or resolving with `--locked` can obtain source metadata without comparing those digests. A replaced source archive can therefore run its build backend before a later hash or lockfile check rejects it. Construct a `HashStrategy` from the existing lockfile's hashes for registry packages, direct URLs, and local archives. Enforce the recorded hashes when reusing cached source metadata, resolving with `--locked`, and installing build dependencies recorded in the lockfile into isolated build environments. Normalize equivalent archive subdirectories so they find the same recorded hashes. Keep recorded hashes while checking whether an existing lockfile is still usable, but allow unlocked fresh resolution to replace them. Build dependencies without recorded hashes remain allowed. Based on #21248, which checks source archives before saving them to the cache. #21246 contains the structural refactor, and #21247 separates hash generation from verification.

signal.title: Separate hash generation policy from verification policy
signal.text: `HashStrategy` currently represents hash generation and verification as mutually exclusive choices. A resolution may need both: verify artifacts whose hashes have been supplied, while generating hashes for new artifacts. Store generation separately from `HashVerification` in `HashStrategy`. Each distribution still receives a `HashPolicy` specifying whether to generate or check hashes. Update existing call sites to use the separate settings while preserving their hash inputs and which hashes uv treats as trusted. Generation remains available for artifacts without supplied hashes, unless the caller requires a hash for every artifact. This does not read hashes from `uv.lock` or add new archive comparisons. Based on #21246. #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before source archives enter the cache. #21223 reads hashes from an existing `uv.lock` and supplies them for verification.

signal.title: Represent validated source archives before persistence
signal.text: Source archive helpers currently extract an archive and save it to the cache in the same call. Separate those steps so the type system records that extraction and its existing checks have completed before persistence. Introduce a private `ValidatedSourceArchive` that owns the temporary directory. Its HTTP and local constructors retain their transport setup, diagnostics, and cleanup behavior, while a private reader helper performs the shared extraction and hash collection. The consuming `persist` method saves the source tree and returns the collected hashes and byte count. This preserves existing behavior; it does not add trusted-hash comparisons or change cache repair. #21247 separates hash generation from verification, and #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before persistence.

signal.title: Support proxy indexes through reversible artifact URLs
signal.text: Add support for using a proxy for an existing package index without changing the URLs stored in lockfiles. Configure proxies on ordinary `[[tool.uv.index]]` or `[[index]]` entries with `proxy-for` and `artifact-base-url`. PyPI works without additional configuration; other indexes must specify where their artifacts are hosted. uv resolves and downloads packages through the proxy, but stores the original URLs in `uv.lock` and `pylock.toml`. When installing from an existing lockfile, it converts those original URLs back into proxy URLs. Authentication, errors, and caches belong to the proxy. Artifact hashes are checked before files are cached or written to lockfiles. Frozen and offline installs continue to work. ## Terminology - **Proxy index:** An index configured with `proxy-for` that serves packages for another index. - **Canonical index:** The original index whose identity and artifact URLs appear in lockfiles. - **Physical index:** The index uv contacts for requests, authentication, and caching. This is the proxy when one is configured. - **Artifact base URL:** The URL prefix where an index hosts package files, configured with `artifact-base-url`. - **Proxy route:** The connection between a canonical index and its physical index. - **Artifact URL mapping:** The reversible conversion between canonical and physical artifact URLs that preserves the path after each artifact base URL. ## Commit breakdown 1. **Define proxy indexes and reversible artifact routes.** Add the configuration options and schema. Validate proxy definitions, reject duplicates, support implicit PyPI, and map artifact URLs between the original index and its proxy. 2. **Route registry requests through proxies.** Send package and metadata requests to the proxy. Use its authentication settings, credentials, errors, and cache. Artifact hosts requiring separate credentials must specify them explicitly. 3. **Preserve canonical package URLs during proxy resolution.** Convert artifact URLs returned by the proxy into their original URLs before the resolver sees them. signal.title: Preserve repository-relative Git archive paths during sync
signal.text: Fresh `uv sync` can look for a Git-hosted archive in the downstream project instead of the Git checkout, even though retrying with the written lockfile succeeds. Source history traces this to astral-sh/uv#10072: it introduced repository-relative `GitPathBuiltDist::install_path` and `GitPathSourceDist::install_path`, but their lock constructors applied `relative_to` against the workspace root and fell back to `std::path::absolute`. `locked_git_url` retained the original relative path, so the serialized lock was correct while the in-memory `GitSource.path` used by the first sync was not. The direct-archive tests locked before installing. Later, astral-sh/uv#19589 preserved Git identity when lowering generated metadata that references an archive in the same checkout, but its regression only inspected the lockfile. Neither exercised installation from the newly constructed in-memory lock. Preserve the repository-relative path in both Git archive lock constructors and use it consistently for `locked_git_url` and `GitSource.path`. The installer then resolves the archive inside the fetched Git checkout, so fresh sync and lockfile replay use the same path. Fixes astral-sh/uv#21244.

signal.title: Improve basic space accounting when reporting cache clean space savings
signal.text: ## Summary While looking at Charlie's new preview space accounting PR which utilises special APIs to count extents I noticed we have some areas where small changes could improve accounting accuracy. This PR uses block counts instead of file sizes to determine file space savings and additionally uses hardlink counts to avoid double-counting space when hardlinks are in use. Notably the PR changes a small detail about our output format, it now reports the number of bytes recovered (even if it's zero) whenever any files or directories were deleted. Previously we had some quirky logic where we'd only do this if we had "logical" or "physical" counts, regardless of which one we'd then print. I think the intent is to report 0 when things were deleted but nothing got saved so I picked that as a simpler condition. ## Test Plan Adjustments to existing tests and some new tests. Unit tests avoid some of the potential uncertainty when doing accounting.

signal.text: ### Summary The `uv` and `uvx` tools do not carry a code signature from Astral on macOS, as of version 0.8.2 checked on 2025-07-24 on macOS 15.5. ``` ❯ uv --version uv 0.8.2 (21fadbcc1 2025-07-22) ❯ sw_vers ProductName: macOS ProductVersion: 15.5 BuildVersion: 24F74 ``` I could not find a similar open or closed request regarding adding a macOS code signature to `uv` and `uvx` in the issue tracker. Issue #10366 is a similar request for Windows. Code signing from the developer is preferred and contributes to trust in these tools when running on macOS / Darwin. Code signing could potentially be done with other PKI, but for this request, the best result would be an Apple Developer ID signature. 1. Signing versions of `uv` and `uvx` on macOS would provide proof that the release came from Astral (or Astral’s build/release pipeline). CI/CD pipeline tools offer support for code signing actions. 2. The signature would enable verification that the tools have not been modified since their release. 3. The signature can be used in Apple’s anti-malware / threat protection processes. 4. The valid signature and its Team ID can be used by automation for IT teams, like [AutoPkg](https://github.com/autopkg/autopkg), to verify the downloaded releases when discovering new versions, packaging them, and preparing them for organizational deployments. signal.title: Reimplement `package.metadata`-less lockfiles
signal.text: The previous iterations of `package.metadata`-free lockfiles had missed a number of cases, and made it hard to ensure that all cases were actually covered. This PR takes a new approach: Remove the previous implementation, and then re-add it feature-by-feature in reviewable commit units. Each commit adds one feature that uv supports. The new approach is not entirely `package.metadata`-free, instead remote URL, which can activate other URL source, now have `package.metadata` which they previously didn't. That's required for offline validation (which is crucial for `uv lock --check` performance, offline or not) and IMO the more correct tradeoff: We shouldn't repeat information that's already available on disk, but we should state what we expect from remote resources. `uv.lock` revision 1.4 additionally records empty extras so `--frozen --extra foo` if the lock wasn't generated with extra `foo` present, but it was added to `pyproject.toml` afterwards. This is a lockfile size regression if you're using a lot of remote URLs, otherwise it's still a much smaller lockfile for large workspaces. Remote source are usually used sparingly as they are worse for performance, reliability and auditability than registry sources. ## Validation This change reflects basically every resolver assumption and form of dependency specification and also hits a number of preexisting bugs (see upstack PRs and skipped changes list). Instead of trying to reason through correctness from the features we're representing, this PR was tested (and fixed) against large, diverse validation set, checking that uv's invariants are upheld with lockfile revision 1.4. The PR is additionally split into one commit per feature the new freshness check support, to ease reviewing and ensure that all features are covered. The most import check that needs to always pass is `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` on a fresh lockfile. We don't need to check features such as `uv sync`, as `package.metadata` is only used for fast path freshness checks, and `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` exercises the offline fast path while blocking the slow path if it would use the internet (which is unacceptable both for performance and for checks that run in isolated environments). The goal is to cover the available dependency specification that people use, while not fixing unrelated bugs in this already large change. There are three of these larger validations. The first one is a script finds public GitHub projects with editable packages, workspaces, Git dependencies or dynamically generated dependencies and then verifies that both the original lockfile and a version with package metadata removed pass `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` inside an isolated docker container. This dataset contained 254 projects with 14k locked packages. The second validation uses the check-mode in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-ecosystem-testing with `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=lock-without-metadata` . The third one is running the test suite migrated to lockfile revision 1.4 with https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/4b98802626b18406a47e71fc2583bc5576934e6e, passing 4.8k tests: ``` features=test-python-patch,test-universal,native-auth cargo insta test --accept --test-runner nextest --workspace --features "$features" cargo nextest run --workspace --features "$features" ``` The PR handles the test cases and fixes from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/20803 too. The area with the least coverage wrt to its complexity is conflicts supports. While the support is implemented, I'd consider its current support much weaker than the rest of the features. ## Skipped changes The following independent bugfixes are deliberately excluded from this stack: - #21210. - #21225. The cache assertion remains a TODO here. The 4.8k-test run above included the add-cache fix and predates this extraction; it is not a fresh full-suite run of the reduced stack.

signal.title: Allow an empty metadata cache when adding lower bounds
signal.text: Stacked on #21163. Reusing a metadata-free lock can leave the in-memory distribution index empty. When `uv add` inserts a lower bound and locks again, invalidating the project's metadata must tolerate an entry that was never cached. Remove the cache-presence assertion and extend the existing lower-bound regression test to cover adding a redundant marker after reusing a metadata-free lock.

signal.title: `uv sync` with `--no-editable` should force rebuild/install packages
signal.text: ### Summary When running `uv sync` with `--no-editable`, it seems like we'd expect that we re-install packages that would've been installed as editable (for example, the main package). Here's a simple example: ```shellsession jrosenth ~/example-project % uv init --build-backend uv Initialized project `example-project` jrosenth ~/example-project % uv sync --no-editable Using CPython 3.13.0 Creating virtual environment at: .venv Resolved 1 package in 2ms Built example-project @ file:///home/jrosenth/example-project Prepared 1 package in 15ms Installed 1 package in 1ms + example-project==0.1.0 (from file:///home/jrosenth/example-project) jrosenth ~/example-project % echo 'print("changed!")' >> src/example_project/__init__.py jrosenth ~/example-project % uv sync --no-editable Resolved 1 package in 0.88ms Audited 1 package in 0.04ms jrosenth ~/example-project % tail .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/example_project/__init__.py def main() -> None: print("Hello from example-project!") jrosenth ~/example-project % uv sync --no-editable --reinstall-package example-project Resolved 1 package in 0.94ms Built example-project @ file:///home/jrosenth/example-project Prepared 1 package in 15ms Uninstalled 1 package in 0.40ms Installed 1 package in 1ms ~ example-project==0.1.0 (from file:///home/jrosenth/example-project) jrosenth ~/example-project % tail .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/example_project/__init__.py def main() -> None: print("Hello from example-project!") print("changed!") ``` In this example, we notice the `example-project` package didn't sync local changes until `--reinstall-package` was manually used. With packages that have `path` dependencies, this could be a little bit more fishy, we'd expect each of those dependencies to re-build and re-install when `--no-editable` is applied. ### Platform Linux 6.15.8-arch1-2 x86_64 GNU/Linux ### Version uv 0.8.8 (9a54754b0 2025-08-08) ### Python version Python 3.13

signal.title: uv sync and uv pip install fails for packages with console scripts when the venv contains a `lib` to `usr/lib` symlink
signal.text: ### Summary When a virtual environment directory contains a `lib` to `usr/lib` symlink, `uv` installs `console_scripts` entry points into `<venv>/usr/bin/<name>` instead of the venv's real scripts directory `<venv>/bin/<name>`. The launcher is *written* to a path relative to `site-packages` that traverses the `lib` symlink. This results in the following error: ``` error: Failed to install: idna-3.19-py3-none-any.whl (idna==3.19) Caused by: failed to query metadata of file `<venv>/bin/idna`: No such file or directory (os error 2) ``` ## Reproduction ```bash V=$(mktemp -d)/venv uv venv --allow-existing --python python3.12 "$V" mkdir -p "$V/usr/lib" "$V/usr/bin" ln -s usr/lib "$V/lib" # Install any package that ships a console script (idna provides `idna`). VIRTUAL_ENV="$V" uv pip install idna ls -l "$V/bin/idna" "$V/usr/bin/idna" ``` I suspect that this issue comes from the fact that after writing the console scripts, `uv` makes it executable and a recent change switched from using the relative path of `site_packages` to using the absolute_path: [ref](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/9a65753e9a8d0e99e7079114d78001311444c718#diff-f2224e4fc2200243c3f25811f8f3ea23cda624fab45a26a09f91c47d77aafdb7) ```rust // let path = site_packages.join(entrypoint_relative); let path = script.as_path(); let permissions = fs::metadata(path)?.permissions(); ``` ### Platform Ubuntu ### Version uv 0.12.0 ### Python version Python 3.12
